thread:
ravi: Quick weekly train bulletin: brief policy update + canary note. Please skim.
ravi: Quiet window this weekend: 2024-06-14 22:00 UTC -> 2024-06-15 06:00 UTC. Were adding a hard check: any change that touches runtime scheduling must include a preflight that proves tail-latency bounded for 1h under synthetic load.
haley: What does the preflight look like? Where's the test harness?
ravi: Use infra/tests/preflight/tail_latency_check.sh --service runtime --duration 60m --sample prod. Acceptance: p99 change <= 150ms vs baseline. Upload raw output to the PR.
ops-bot: Note: auto-pause rule updated. If tail latency increases > 120ms for > 5m during ramp, canary will auto-pause.
mike: Heads-up: we paused a small canary earlier today (v6.0-canary) after we saw a scheduling jitter when batch-sizes shifted. No customer impact.
ravi: Thanks Mike. Because of that, were delaying the v6.0 gradual rollout by 12h to allow runtime team to push a micro-fix. If you own the change, add the preflight results and heap/gc snapshots.
mike: Will do. One doc ask: rollout manifests need a new field for "preflight_proof_link". Who updates it?
haley: I'll update deploy/rollout_manifest.md and add a checklist item for release-ops to verify the proof link before unpause.
release-bot: Canary status: v6.0 = PAUSED (manual), v5.9 = STABLE. Quiet window = SCHEDULED. Auto-pause thresholds = UPDATED.
ravi: Recap action items: 1) runtime owners add preflight proof (mike) 2) deploy doc update (haley) 3) ops to monitor tail-latency dashboards during ramp (ops-bot). Hold non-critical merges that touch scheduling until preflight is green.
mike: Copy, starting preflight now; will post results in thread.
ops-bot: Monitoring: dashboards updated to include p99-sched-latency and jitter heatmap. Alerts set for sustained p99 > 120ms over 5m.
ravi: Thanks team. If anyone needs an exception during the quiet window, use #release-ops and include 2 approvers from eng-leads and ops with rollback plan.
